sentences: The sun has set, and only a deep blue light remains over the beach.
A man and a woman stroll arm in arm along the edge of the water.
The sea is as still as glass, the moon lays a long path of light across it, and a dog follows at the man's feet.
This is Summer Evening on Skagen Beach.
The Artist and his Wife, painted in 1899 by the Danish painter P.
S. Krøyer. The two figures are Krøyer himself and his wife, the painter Marie Krøyer, and the dog is their own dog, Rap.
Krøyer was born in Stavanger, Norway, in 1851 and grew up in Denmark.
After studying in Paris, he first came in 1882 to Skagen, a fishing village at the northern tip of Denmark, and soon became the leading figure of the artists who gathered there every summer.
He died in Skagen in 1909.
He married Marie in 1889.
In 1895 he wrote to a friend that he was thinking of painting a large portrait of himself and his wife together, but that he would need good weather for it.
The plan had to wait four more years, until the summer of 1899.
Now look at the sky and the sea.
This is the moment after dusk when everything sinks into shades of blue, often called the blue hour.
From the early 1890s until the end of his life, Krøyer was fascinated by the light of this hour and returned to it again and again.
Follow the moonlight on the water.
Its reflection stretches out in a long, trembling line across the calm surface.
There are hardly any waves, and the whole beach seems to have fallen silent.
Now look at the couple.
They walk side by side with their arms linked, yet they are not looking at each other; both gaze out across the quiet sea.
It is a portrait of a married couple, but each of them seems lost in private thoughts.
Look down at Rap, keeping close beside his master.
Then look to the horizon, where two boats are sailing, one pale and one dark.
Some writers have read the two boats as the different temperaments of husband and wife.
The following year, in 1900, the painting was shown at the spring exhibition in Copenhagen and at the World's Fair in Paris.
Later it travelled to exhibitions in Berlin, London and Venice.
Krøyer's patron, the tobacco manufacturer Heinrich Hirschsprung, became his friend when the artist was still young, and they stayed close for more than thirty years.
The museum built on his collection in Copenhagen holds the largest group of Krøyer's works outside Skagen, including this painting.
Step back and see it whole: the moonlight, the still sea, two people walking side by side.
This evening, after the sun goes down, why not take a short walk with someone close to you?
